While still catching up to men in some spheres of modern life, women appear to be way ahead in at least one undesirable category. “Women are particularly susceptible to developing depression and anxiety disorders in response to stress compared to men,” according to Dr. Yehuda, chief psychiatrist at New York’s Veteran’s Administration Hospital.

Studies of both animals and humans have shown that sex hormones somehow affect the stress response, causing females under stress to produce more of the trigger chemicals than do males under the same conditions. In several of the studies, when stressed-out female rats had their ovaries (the female reproductive organs) removed, their chemical responses became equal to those of the males.

Adding to a woman’s increased dose of stress chemicals, are her increased “opportunities” for stress. “It’s not necessarily that women don’t cope as well. It’s just that they have so much more to cope with,” says Dr. Yehuda. “Their capacity for tolerating stress may even be greater than men’s,” she observes, “it’s just that they’re dealing with so many more things that they become worn out from it more visibly and sooner.”

Dr. Yehuda notes another difference between the sexes. “I think that the kinds of things that women are exposed to tend to be in more of a chronic or repeated nature. Men go to war and are exposed to combat stress. Men are exposed to more acts of random physical violence. The kinds of interpersonal violence that women are exposed to tend to be in domestic situations, by, unfortunately, parents or other family members, and they tend not to be one-shot deals. The wear-and-tear that comes from these longer relationships can be quite devastating.”

Adeline Alvarez married at 18 and gave birth to a son, but was determined to finish college. “I struggled a lot to get the college degree. I was living in so much frustration that that was my escape, to go to school, and get ahead and do better.” Later, her marriage ended and she became a single mother. “It’s the hardest thing to take care of a teenager, have a job, pay the rent, pay the car payment, and pay the debt. I lived from paycheck to paycheck.”

Not everyone experiences the kinds of severe chronic stresses Alvarez describes. But most women today are coping with a lot of obligations, with few breaks, and feeling the strain. Alvarez’s experience demonstrates the importance of finding ways to diffuse stress before it threatens your health and your ability to function.

It used to be so straightforward. A team of researchers working together in the laboratory would submit the results of their research to a journal. A journal editor would then remove the authors’ names and affiliations from the paper and send it to their peers for review. Depending on the comments received, the editor would accept the paper for publication or decline it. Copyright rested with the journal publisher, and researchers seeking knowledge of the results would have to subscribe to the journal.

No longer. The Internet—and pressure from funding agencies, who are questioning why commercial publishers are making money from government-funded research by restricting access to it—is making free access to scientific results a reality. The Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) has just issued a report describing the far-reaching consequences of this. The report, by John Houghton of Victoria University in Australia and Graham Vickery of the OECD, makes heavy reading for publishers who have, so far, made handsome profits. But it goes further than that. It signals a change in what has, until now, been a key element of scientific endeavour.

The value of knowledge and the return on the public investment in research depends, in part, upon wide distribution and ready access. It is big business. In America, the core scientific publishing market is estimated at between $7 billion and $11 billion. The International Association of Scientific, Technical and Medical Publishers says that there are more than 2,000 publishers worldwide specializing in these subjects. They publish more than 1.2 million articles each year in some 16,000 journals.

This is now changing. According to the OECD report, some 75% of scholarly journals are now online. Entirely new business models are emerging; three main ones were identified by the report’s authors. There is the so-called big deal, where institutional subscribers pay for access to a collection of online journal titles through site-licensing agreements. There is open-access publishing, typically supported by asking the author (or his employer) to pay for the paper to be published. Finally, there are open-access archives, where organizations such as universities or international laboratories support institutional repositories. Other models exist that are hybrids of these three, such as delayed open-access, where journals allow only subscribers to read a paper for the first six months, before making it freely available to everyone who wishes to see it. All this could change the traditional form of the peer-review process, at least for the publication of papers.

In the early 1960s Wilt Chamberlain was one of the only three players in the National Basketball Association (NBA) listed at over seven feet. If he had played last season, however, he would have been one of 42. The bodies playing major professional sports have changed dramatically over the years, and managers have been more than willing to adjust team uniforms to fit the growing numbers of bigger, longer frames.

The trend in sports, though, may be obscuring an unrecognized reality: Americans have generally stopped growing. Though typically about two inches taller now than 140 years ago, today’s people—especially those born to families who have lived in the U.S. for many generations—apparently reached their limit in the early 1960s. And they aren’t likely to get any taller. “In the general population today, at this genetic, environmental level, we’ve pretty much gone as far as we can go,” says anthropologist William Cameron Chumlea of Wright State University. In the case of NBA players, their increase in height appears to result from the increasingly common practice of recruiting players from all over the world.

Growth, which rarely continues beyond the age of 20, demands calories and nutrients—notably, protein—to feed expanding tissues. At the start of the 20th century, under-nutrition and childhood infections got in the way. But as diet and health improved, children and adolescents have, on average, increased in height by about an inch and a half every 20 years, a pattern known as the secular trend in height. Yet according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, average height—5′9″ for men, 5′4″ for women—hasn’t really changed since 1960.

Genetically speaking, there are advantages to avoiding substantial height. During childbirth, larger babies have more difficulty passing through the birth canal. Moreover, even though humans have been upright for millions of years, our feet and back continue to struggle with bipedal posture and cannot easily withstand repeated strain imposed by oversize limbs. “There are some real constraints that are set by the genetic architecture of the individual organism,” says anthropologist William Leonard of Northwestern University.

Genetic maximums can change, but don’t expect this to happen soon. Claire C. Gordon, senior anthropologist at the Army Research Center in Natick, Mass., ensures that 90 percent of the uniforms and workstations fit recruits without alteration. She says that, unlike those for basketball, the length of military uniforms has not changed for some time. And if you need to predict human height in the near future to design a piece of equipment, Gordon says that by and large, “you could use today’s data and feel fairly confident.”

In 1784, five years before he became president of the United States, George Washington, 52, was nearly toothless. So he hired a dentist to transplant nine teeth into his jaw—having extracted them from the mouths of his slaves.

That’s a far different image from the cherry-tree-chopping George most people remember from their history books. But recently, many historians have begun to focus on the role slavery played in the lives of the founding generation. They have been spurred in part by DNA evidence made available in 1998, which almost certainly proved Thomas Jefferson had fathered at least one child with his slave Sally Hemings. And only over the past 30 years have scholars examined history from the bottom up. Works of several historians reveal the moral compromises made by the nation’s early leaders and the fragile nature of the country’s infancy. More significantly, they argue that many of the Founding Fathers knew slavery was wrong—and yet most did little to fight it.

More than anything, the historians say, the founders were hampered by the culture of their time. While Washington and Jefferson privately expressed distaste for slavery, they also understood that it was part of the political and economic bedrock of the country they helped to create.

For one thing, the South could not afford to part with its slaves. Owning slaves was “like having a large bank account,” says Wiencek, author of An Imperfect God: George Washington, His Slaves, and the Creation of America. The southern states would not have signed the Constitution without protections for the “peculiar institution,” including a clause that counted a slave as three fifths of a man for purposes of congressional representation.

And the statesmen’s political lives depended on slavery. The three-fifths formula handed Jefferson his narrow victory in the presidential election of 1800 by inflating the votes of the southern states in the Electoral College. Once in office, Jefferson extended slavery with the Louisiana Purchase in 1803; the new land was carved into 13 states, including three slave states.

Still, Jefferson freed Hemings’s children—though not Hemings herself or his approximately 150 other slaves. Washington, who had begun to believe that all men were created equal after observing the bravery of the black soldiers during the Revolutionary War, overcame the strong opposition of his relatives to grant his slaves their freedom in his will. Only a decade earlier, such an act would have required legislative approval in Virginia.

map: introduced a credit limit
PRH’s business move
remove … from prominent areas
respond to

questions.stem: What message does the spokesperson for Waterstones seem to convey?

options.B: The credit limit will be removed.
options.C: Their stock is underestimated.
options.D: The book market is rather slack.

questions.answerZh: 信用额度限制将被取消
basis: 发言人说希望“恢复正常”、希望“能被允许合理进货”。现在之所以不能合理进货，是因为企鹅兰登收紧了信用条款；恢复正常就意味着这个限制被取消。后面说书店异常忙碌、五月销量创 2018 年以来新高，是在给这个期待找理由：我们生意很好，没理由被限制。题干用 seem to convey，问的正是这种言外之意。
map: normality will return
the credit limit will be removed
be allowed to buy appropriately
removed

context.text: ==In the meantime, PRH authors have been **the losers**.== Big-name PRH authors may suffer a bit, but ==it’s those **mid-list authors**, who normally **rely on** Waterstones staff’s passion for promoting books by lesser-known writers, who will be **praying for an end to the dispute**==.

questions.stem: What can be one consequence of the current dispute?

map: have been the losers
fall off
mid-list authors … praying for an end to the dispute
mid-list PRH writers … considerably

店员的热情是推荐不太知名的作家；大牌作者“受点影响”是因为纠纷，不是店员犹豫推荐。

==“This is all part of a **wider change towards concentration of power**,”== says literary agent Andrew Lownie. …

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best represents Lownie’s view?

options.A: Small publishers ought to stick together.

options.C: The publishing industry is having a hard time.

questions.answerZh: 出版商合并是一种令人担忧的趋势
basis: 第五段说作者们担心企鹅兰登与西蒙与舒斯特拟议中的合并：独立出版商变少，竞价减少、预付款降低、出版内容趋同。Lownie 接着说“这都是权力日益集中这一更大变化的一部分”，并强调出版业需要多元、好书多出自小出版商。合并造成权力集中，他对此显然是担忧的。
map: a wider change towards concentration of power
a … trend
worried about … the proposed merger
the merger of publishers is … worrying

context.text: … ==The careers of scientists and the reputation of their institutions **depend on** the number and prestige of the papers they produce, but **even more so on the citations attracted by these papers**.==

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, the careers of scientists can be determined by ______.

options.A: how many citations their works contain
options.B: how many times their papers are cited
options.C: the prestige of the people they work with
options.D: the status they have in scientific circles

questions.answerZh: 他们的论文被引用了多少次
basis: 第一段最后一句：科学家的职业生涯取决于论文的数量和声望，“更取决于这些论文吸引到的引用”。citations attracted by these papers 是别人引用这些论文，也就是被引次数。
map: depend on
can be determined by
the citations attracted by these papers
how many times their papers are cited

wrong.text: “论文里包含多少引用”是引用别人，原文说的是论文“吸引到”的引用，即被别人引用。
原文说的是论文的声望(prestige of the papers)，不是合作者的声望。
原文提到的是机构的声誉，没有说科学家个人在学界的地位。

context.text: … Recently, another expression of this predatory behavior has emerged: ==so-called support service consultancies that provide language and other editorial support to individual authors and to journals sometimes **advise contributors to add a number of citations** to their articles==.

questions.stem: The support service consultancies tend to ______.

options.B: list citation patterns for their clients
options.C: ask authors to include extra citations
options.D: advise contributors to cite each other

questions.answerZh: 要求作者加入额外的引用
basis: 第二段最后一句直接给出：这些所谓的支持服务咨询公司“有时会建议投稿人在文章里加上若干引用”。add a number of citations 就是额外加引用。
map: advise contributors to add a number of citations
ask authors to include extra citations

wrong.text: 没说咨询公司给客户推荐期刊。
识别“引用模式”的是 2016 年研究人员开发的算法，不是咨询公司。
“互相引用”(cite one another) 说的是引用卡特尔里的作者群和期刊群，咨询公司是让作者加引用，没说互相引用。

context.text: … ==These journals can act as milk cows where **every single article in an issue may cite a specific paper** or a series of papers.== In some instances, there is absolutely no relationship between the content of the article and the citations. The peculiar part is that the journal that the editor is supposedly working for is not profiting at all—it is just providing citations to other journals. ==Such practices can lead an article to **accrue more than 150 citations** in the same year that it was published.==

questions.stem: The function of the “milk cow” journals is to ______.

options.A: boost citation counts for certain authors
options.B: help scholars publish articles at low cost
options.C: instruct first-time contributors in citation
options.D: increase the readership of new journals

questions.answerZh: 为某些作者刷高引用数
basis: “摇钱树”期刊的特点是一期里的每篇文章都去引用某一篇或某一系列论文，哪怕内容毫不相干；期刊本身不获利，只是给别的期刊“提供引用”；结果一篇文章发表当年就能攒到 150 多次引用。它们的作用就是给特定的论文和作者刷引用。
map: may cite a specific paper or a series of papers
for certain authors
accrue more than 150 citations
boost citation counts
questions.note: milk cow 字面是“奶牛”，比喻被不断“挤”出好处的对象，译作“摇钱树”：这里被挤出来的就是引用。

wrong.text: 没提发表成本。
没提指导新作者如何引用。
这些期刊“提供引用”给别人，自己并不获利，与扩大读者群无关。

context.text: … ==The problem is **rampant in Scopus**, a citation database, which includes a high number of the new “international” journals.== In fact, a listing in Scopus seems to be a criterion to be targeted in this type of citation manipulation.
==Scopus itself **has all the data necessary to detect** this malpractice.== ==**Red flags** include a large number of citations to an article within the first year.== …

questions.stem: What can be learned about Scopus from the last two paragraphs?

options.A: It fosters competition among citation providers.
options.B: It has the capability to identify suspicious citations.
options.C: It hinders the growth of “international” journals.
options.D: It is established to prevent citation manipulation.

questions.answerZh: 它有能力识别可疑引用
basis: 第四段说引用操纵在 Scopus 里很猖獗；第五段话锋一转：Scopus 本身就掌握了发现这种舞弊所需的全部数据，比如一篇文章发表第一年就被大量引用，就是危险信号。有数据、有信号，就是有能力识别可疑引用。
map: has all the data necessary to detect
has the capability to identify
this malpractice / red flags
suspicious citations

wrong.text: 没提引用提供方之间的竞争。
Scopus 收录了大量新的“国际”期刊，不是阻碍它们发展。
Scopus 是引文数据库，问题恰恰在里面泛滥，没说它为防操纵而建。

context.text: … And for authors who wish to steer clear of citation cartel activities: ==when an editor, a reviewer, or a support service asks you to add inappropriate references, do not oblige and **do report the request to the journal**==.

questions.stem: What should an author do to deal with citation manipulators?

options.C: Seek professional advice.

questions.answerZh: 揭露他们的不当行为
basis: 最后一句给作者的建议：有人要求加不当引用时，不要照办，并且“一定要向期刊举报这一要求”。do report 是强调形式。举报就是揭露对方的不当行为。

context.text: … But some plastic materials change over time. They crack and frizzle. They “weep” out additives. They melt into sludge. ==All of which creates **huge headaches** for institutions, such as museums, **trying to preserve** culturally important objects.== The variety of plastic objects at risk is dizzying: early radios, avant-garde sculptures, celluloid animation stills from Disney films, the first artificial heart.

options.C: handling outdated plastic exhibits

basis: 第一段先说人们抱怨塑料太耐用，接着用 But 转折：有些塑料会随时间变化，开裂、渗出添加剂、融成烂泥。这些变化给博物馆这类想要保存重要文物的机构带来了巨大麻烦（huge headaches）。难在“保存”，就是难在维护塑料藏品。

difficulties
trying to preserve culturally important objects
maintaining their plastic items

这些藏品是文化上重要的物品，没说它们过时。

context.text: Unfortunately, the polyurethane foam he used is inherently unstable. ==It’s especially **vulnerable to light damage**==, and by the mid-1990s, Gilardi’s pumpkins, roses, and other figures were splitting and crumbling. ==Museums **locked some of them away in the dark**.==

challenging

context.text: … Joana Lia Ferreira, an assistant professor of conservation and restoration at the NOVA School of Science and Technology, notes that ==archaeologists first defined the great material ages of human history—Stone Age, Iron Age, and so on—**after examining artifacts in museums**==. We now live in an age of plastic, she says, ==“and what we decide to collect today, what we decide to preserve...**will have a strong impact on how in the future we’ll be seen**.”==

questions.stem: In Ferreira’s opinion, preservation of plastic artifacts ______.

context.text: … ==it may be worth considering just how **the point, purpose and value of a degree has changed**== and what Generation Z need to consider as they start the third stage of their educational journey.

questions.stem: The author suggests that Generation Z should ______.

basis: 首段建议 Z 世代在填申请时想一想：学位的意义、目的和价值已经变了。第三段说得更直接：学位不适合所有人，从中学教室进入大学讲堂不是必然的，还有别的选择。这就是让他们重新评估上大学是否必要。

context.text: ==**Enlightening, challenging, stimulating, fun**.== These were some of the words that Nature readers used to describe their experience of art-science collaborations in a series of articles on partnerships between artists and researchers. context.text: Just how people think is ==still **far too complex** to be understood, **let alone reproduced**==, says David Eagleman, a Stanford University neuroscientist. “We are just in a situation where ==there are **no good theories** explaining what consciousness actually is== and how you could ever build a machine to get there.”

map: far too complex to be understood, let alone reproduced

context.text: … The coming use of autonomous vehicles, for example, ==poses **thorny ethical questions**==. Human drivers sometimes must make split-second decisions. context.text: ==This **isn’t to be alarmist**==. Optimists point out that technological upheaval has benefited workers in the past. Likewise, automation should eventually boost productivity, stimulate demand by driving down prices, and free workers from hard, boring work. Technology will improve society in ways big and small over the next few years, yet this will be little comfort to those who find their lives and careers upended by automation. options.D: preventing the income gap from widening

questions.answerZh: 防止收入差距扩大
basis: 第六段：因为自动化可能拉大资本收入和劳动收入之间的差距（widen the gap），所以要重新考虑税收和社会保障：减少对低收入劳动的征税，扩大工资补贴，这样能提高收入、鼓励工作，并减少不平等。税收政策的目的是防止收入差距扩大。
map: threatens to widen the gap / reduce inequality
preventing the income gap from widening

wrong.text: 原文没说用税收鼓励自动化发展。
作者主张减少低收入劳动的税、增加工资补贴，不是提高资本投资回报。
原文说的是减少收入不平等，没说贫富之间有敌意。

context.text: ==**The first step**==, as Erik Brynjolfsson and Andrew McAfee argue in The Second Machine Age, should be rethinking education and job training. …
==**Finally**, because automation threatens== to widen the gap between capital income and labor income, taxes and the safety net will have to be rethought. …

questions.stem: In this text, the author presents a problem with ______.

options.C: its alarming impacts

questions.answerZh: 给出了可能的解决方案
basis: 前三段提出问题：机器人要来抢中产阶级的工作，中产阶级工人需要很多帮助来调整。第四到六段用 The first step … Finally 依次提出办法：改革教育和职业培训，让创办新公司更容易，重新考虑税收和社会保障。末段强调帮助工人适应的政策必不可少。作者是提出问题，再给出可能的解决办法。
map: The first step … Finally
possible solutions to it

wrong.text: 第三段提到乐观者的看法，只是一笔带过，不是全文的写法。
自动化的影响只在前几段，全文重点在解决办法。
原文没讲这个问题有哪些主要变化。

context.text: … The implication is that Millennials prefer news from the White House to be filtered through other sources, ==**not a president’s social media platform**==.

Most Americans rely on social media to check daily headlines. Yet ==as **distrust has risen toward all media**==, people may be starting to beef up their media literacy skills. Such a trend is badly needed. During the 2016 presidential campaign, nearly a quarter of web content shared by Twitter users in the politically critical state of Michigan was fake news, according to the University of Oxford. And a survey conducted for BuzzFeed News found 44 percent of Facebook users ==**rarely or never trust** news from the media giant==.

questions.stem: According to Paragraphs 1 and 2, many young Americans cast doubts on ______.

options.A: the justification of the news-filtering practice
options.B: people’s preference for social media platforms
options.C: the administration’s ability to handle information
options.D: social media as a reliable source of news

questions.answerZh: 社交媒体作为可靠新闻来源
basis: 第一段：超过三分之二的美国年轻人不赞成特朗普用推特，说明他们更愿意白宫的消息经过其他渠道过滤，而不是来自总统的社交媒体。第二段：人们对所有媒体越来越不信任，密歇根州推特上近四分之一的内容是假新闻，44% 的脸书用户很少或从不相信脸书上的新闻。年轻人怀疑的是社交媒体作为新闻来源的可靠性。
map: not a president’s social media platform / rarely or never trust
social media as a reliable source of news

wrong.text: 年轻人希望白宫的消息经过其他渠道过滤，是认可过滤，不是怀疑它。
原文说多数美国人靠社交媒体看新闻，年轻人怀疑的不是这种偏好，而是社交媒体新闻是否可信。
年轻人不赞成的是总统用推特，原文没说政府处理信息的能力。

context.text: … Yet as distrust has risen toward all media, ==people may be starting to **beef up** their media literacy skills==. ==Such a trend is **badly needed**==. …

questions.stem: The phrase “beef up” (Para. 2) is closest in meaning to ______.

options.C: boast

questions.answerZh: 使敏锐；加强
basis: 第二段：随着人们对所有媒体越来越不信任，人们可能开始 beef up 自己的媒体素养；这种趋势非常必要，因为社交媒体上假新闻很多。对媒体不信任，自然要加强辨别能力，beef up 意思是加强、提高，与 sharpen（使敏锐、提高）最接近。
map: beef up their media literacy skills
sharpen

wrong.text: define 是定义，放进原句说不通。
boast 是夸耀，与“这种趋势非常必要”的语气不符。
share 是分享，原文说的是提高自己的能力，不是分享。

context.text: … A Knight Foundation focus-group survey of young people between ages 14 and 24 found ==they use “distributed trust” to **verify stories**==. ==They **cross-check sources** and prefer news from **different perspectives**==—especially those that are open about any bias. …

questions.stem: According to the Knight Foundation survey, young people ______.

options.A: tend to voice their opinions in cyberspace
options.B: verify news by referring to diverse sources
options.C: have a strong sense of responsibility
options.D: like to exchange views on “distributed trust”

questions.answerZh: 通过参考多种来源核实新闻
basis: 第三段：奈特基金会的调查发现，14 到 24 岁的年轻人用“分布式信任”来核实新闻（verify stories）：他们交叉核对信息来源（cross-check sources），喜欢来自不同视角的新闻。也就是参考多种来源来核实新闻。
map: cross-check sources / verify stories
verify news by referring to diverse sources

wrong.text: 原文没说年轻人喜欢在网上发表意见。
调查结论说的是年轻人对自我教育、主动寻找对立观点负有责任，是为了说明他们怎样核实信息，不是泛泛说他们责任感强。
“分布式信任”是年轻人核实新闻的方法，不是他们讨论的话题。

context.text: … A survey by Barna research group found ==the top reason given by Americans for the fake news phenomenon is **“reader error,”**== more so than made-up stories or factual mistakes in reporting. About a third say the problem of fake news ==lies in “**misinterpretation** or exaggeration of actual news”== via social media. …

questions.stem: The Barna survey found that a main cause for the fake news problem is ______.

options.C: readers’ misinterpretation

questions.answerZh: 读者的误解
basis: 第五段：巴纳的调查发现，美国人认为假新闻现象的首要原因是“读者失误”（reader error），比编造的故事和报道失实更重要；约三分之一的人说问题在于通过社交媒体“误读或夸大真实新闻”。主要原因是读者的误读。
map: “reader error” / misinterpretation
readers’ misinterpretation

wrong.text: 原文提到用户转发新闻是在表达自己的价值观，没说读者的价值观过时。
原文没说记者的报道有偏见。
原文说读者失误比编造的故事更是主要原因。

context.text: Young people who are digital natives ==are indeed becoming **more skillful** at separating fact from fiction in cyberspace==. …
So when young people are critical of an over-tweeting president, ==they reveal a mental discipline in **thinking skills**—and in their choices on **when to share on social media**==.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the best title for the text?

options.A: A Rise in Critical Skills for Sharing News Online
options.B: A Counteraction Against the Over-tweeting Trend
options.C: The Accumulation of Mutual Trust on Social Media
options.D: The Platforms for Projection of Personal Interests

questions.answerZh: 在线分享新闻的关键技能的提高
basis: 全文从年轻人不赞成总统用推特说起，指出人们开始提高媒体素养（第二段），年轻人越来越善于在网上分辨真假（第三段），社交媒体让用户更注意自己转发信息的作用，假新闻的关键在于读者是否转发（第五段），最后说年轻人在思维能力和何时在社交媒体上分享方面表现出自律。中心是网上分享新闻的辨别能力在提高。
map: more skillful / thinking skills … when to share
A Rise in Critical Skills for Sharing News Online

wrong.text: 批评总统发推太多只是开头和结尾的例子，不是全文中心。
“分布式信任”是核实新闻的方法，原文没说社交媒体上互信在积累。
转发新闻表达个人价值观和兴趣只是第五段的一句话。

context.text: … It is against that background that the information commissioner, Elizabeth Denham, has issued her damning verdict against the Royal Free hospital trust under the NHS, which handed over to DeepMind the records of 1.6 million patients in 2015 ==on the basis of a vague agreement which **took far too little account of the patients’ rights**== and their expectations of privacy.

questions.stem: What is true of the agreement between the NHS and DeepMind?

options.A: It caused conflicts among tech giants.
options.B: It failed to pay due attention to patients’ rights.
options.C: It fell short of the latter’s expectations.
options.D: It put both sides into a dangerous situation.

questions.answerZh: 它未能对患者权利给予应有的关注
basis: 第一段末：信息专员德纳姆对皇家自由医院信托作出严厉裁决，因为它在 2015 年依据一份模糊的协议，把 160 万名患者的病历交给了 DeepMind，而这份协议对患者的权利和隐私期望考虑得太少（took far too little account of）。也就是没有充分重视患者的权利。
map: took far too little account of the patients’ rights
It failed to pay due attention to patients’ rights.

wrong.text: 原文说可能让权力进一步集中到科技巨头手中，不是在科技巨头之间引发冲突。
协议没顾及的是患者的期望，不是 DeepMind 的期望。
原文说要先承认双方本意是好的，没说协议让双方陷入危险。

context.text: DeepMind has almost apologized. ==The NHS trust has **mended its ways**==. Further arrangements —and there may be many—between the NHS and DeepMind ==will be **carefully scrutinised**== to ensure that all necessary permissions have been asked of patients and all unnecessary data has been cleaned. …

questions.stem: The NHS trust responded to Denham’s verdict with ______.

options.C: necessary adjustments

questions.answerZh: 必要的调整
basis: 第二段：DeepMind 差不多已经道歉，NHS 的这个信托已经改正了做法（mended its ways）。今后双方的合作都会受到仔细审查，确保征得患者的必要许可，删除不必要的数据。信托对裁决的回应是作出必要的调整。
map: has mended its ways
necessary adjustments

wrong.text: 信托已经改正了做法，不是空口许诺。
信托接受了裁决并改正，没有强硬抵制。
差不多道了歉的是 DeepMind，不是 NHS 信托。

context.text: … But privacy is not the only angle in this case and not even the most important. Ms Denham chose to concentrate the blame on the NHS trust, since under existing law it “controlled” the data and DeepMind merely “processed” it. But this distinction misses the point that ==it is **processing and aggregation**, not the mere possession of bits, that **gives the data value**==.

questions.stem: The author argues in Paragraph 2 that ______.

options.A: privacy protection must be secured at all costs
options.B: leaking patients’ data is worse than selling it
options.C: making profits from patients’ data is illegal
options.D: the value of data comes from the processing of it

questions.answerZh: 数据的价值来自于对它的处理
basis: 第二段后半：隐私不是本案唯一的角度，甚至不是最重要的。德纳姆把责任集中在 NHS 信托上，因为按现行法律，信托“控制”数据，DeepMind 只是“处理”数据。作者认为这种区分没有抓住要点：让数据有价值的，是处理和汇总数据，而不是单纯拥有数据。
map: processing and aggregation … gives the data value
the value of data comes from the processing of it

wrong.text: 作者说隐私不是唯一的角度，甚至不是最重要的。
原文没有比较泄露和出售患者数据。
原文没说用患者数据赚钱是违法的。

context.text: … ==This practice does not address **the real worry**==. It is not enough to say that the algorithms DeepMind develops will benefit patients and save lives. What matters is that ==they will belong to **a private monopoly** which developed them using public resources==. If software promises to save lives on the scale that drugs now can, big data may be expected to behave as a big pharma has done. We are still at the beginning of this revolution and small choices now may turn out to have gigantic consequences later. A long struggle will be needed ==to avoid a future of **digital feudalism**==. …

questions.stem: According to the last paragraph, the real worry arising from this deal is ______.

options.A: the vicious rivalry among big pharmas
options.B: the ineffective enforcement of privacy law
options.C: the uncontrolled use of new software
options.D: the monopoly of big data by tech giants

questions.answerZh: 科技巨头对大数据的垄断
basis: 最后一段：用隐私法约束科技巨头不太对路，解决不了真正的担忧（the real worry）。重要的是，DeepMind 开发的算法将属于一家私人垄断企业，而它是用公共资源开发出来的；作者还警告要避免“数字封建主义”的未来。真正的担忧是科技巨头垄断大数据。
map: belong to a private monopoly / digital feudalism
the monopoly of big data by tech giants

wrong.text: big pharma 只是类比，说大数据可能像大药企那样行事，不是说药企之间恶性竞争。
作者说用隐私法约束科技巨头不太对路，不是说隐私法执行不力。
作者担心的是算法被私人垄断，不是新软件被滥用。

context.text: … ==The potential of this work applied to healthcare is **very great**, but it could also lead to **further concentration of power** in the tech giants==. …
… We are still at the beginning of this revolution and ==small choices now may turn out to have **gigantic consequences** later==. …

questions.stem: The author’s attitude toward the application of AI to healthcare is ______.

options.C: appreciative

questions.answerZh: 谨慎的
basis: 第一段：人工智能用于医疗潜力很大，但也可能让权力进一步集中到科技巨头手中。最后一段：这场革命才刚开始，现在的小选择以后可能产生巨大后果，要经过长期斗争才能避免数字封建主义。作者既看到好处，也提醒风险，态度是谨慎的。
map: very great, but … / small choices … gigantic consequences
cautious

wrong.text: 作者立场很清楚：肯定潜力，也警惕垄断，并不含糊。
作者只在开头肯定了潜力，全文重点在提醒风险。
作者承认潜力巨大，没有轻视。

context.text: … Fundamentally, the USPS is in a historic squeeze between technological change that has permanently decreased demand for its bread-and-butter product, first-class mail, and ==a regulatory structure that **denies management the flexibility** to adjust its operations to the new reality==.

questions.stem: The financial problem with the USPS is caused partly by ______.

options.C: the cost for technical upgrading

questions.answerZh: 其僵化的管理
basis: 第一段末：从根本上说，美国邮政夹在两者之间：一是技术变化永久减少了对其主打产品一类邮件的需求，二是监管体制不给管理层灵活调整经营、适应新现实的余地（denies management the flexibility）。管理缺乏灵活性，就是管理僵化。
map: denies management the flexibility
its rigid management

wrong.text: 连续多年支出大于收入是财务问题本身，不是造成问题的原因。

原文没提银行停止支持。

context.text: And ==interest groups ranging from postal unions to greeting-card makers **exert self-interested pressure**== on the USPS’s ultimate overseer—Congress—insisting that whatever else happens to the Postal Service, aspects of the status quo they depend on get protected. ==**This is why** repeated attempts at reform legislation have failed== in recent years, leaving the Postal Service unable to pay its bills ==except by **deferring vital modernization**==.

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 2, the USPS fails to modernize itself due to ______.

options.C: the shrinking demand for postal service

questions.answerZh: 利益集团的干预
basis: 第二段：从邮政工会到贺卡制造商的各种利益集团，出于私利向国会施压，坚持要保护它们依赖的现状。这就是（This is why）近年来改革立法屡屡失败的原因，结果邮政只能靠推迟至关重要的现代化来支付账单。无法现代化是因为利益集团的干预。
map: exert self-interested pressure … This is why
the interference from interest groups

wrong.text: 原文说利益集团向国会施压，没说国会拨款不足。
需求萎缩是第一段讲的财务困境原因，不是第二段说的无法现代化的原因。
邮政工会只是利益集团之一，原文也没说它无能。

context.text: … Most of the money would come from a penny-per-letter permanent rate increase and from shifting postal retirees into Medicare. ==The latter step would largely **offset the financial burden of annually pre-funding retiree health care**, thus **addressing a long-standing complaint**== by the USPS and its unions.

questions.stem: The long-standing complaint by the USPS and its unions can be addressed by ______.

options.A: removing its burden of retiree health care
options.B: making more investment in new vehicles
options.C: adopting a new rate-increase mechanism

questions.answerZh: 减轻其退休人员医疗保健的负担
basis: 第三段：省下的钱主要来自两处，一是每封信永久涨价一美分，二是把邮政退休人员转入联邦医疗保险（Medicare）。后一项能大大抵消每年预先支付退休人员医保的财务负担，从而解决（addressing）美国邮政及其工会长期以来的抱怨。
map: offset the financial burden of … retiree health care
removing its burden of retiree health care

wrong.text: 买新车是省下的钱的用途之一，与长期抱怨无关。
涨价是钱的另一个来源，解决长期抱怨的是后一项措施。

questions.stem: In the last paragraph, the author seems to view legislators with ______.

options.C: discontent

questions.answerZh: 不满
basis: 最后一段末：围绕法案形成的共识，说明立法者害怕邮政在短期内崩溃让他们在政治上难堪；然而这并不说明他们开始认真考虑让邮政系统面向 21 世纪转型。只顾眼前、不想长远，作者对立法者是不满的。
map: It is not, however, a sign that they’re getting serious
discontent

wrong.text: 作者批评立法者只怕难堪、不认真改革，谈不上尊重。
作者对立法者的做法是批评，不是宽容。
作者没有感激立法者。

context.text: If it clears the House, this measure would still have to get through the Senate—where someone is bound to point out that ==it amounts to the **bare, bare minimum** necessary to keep the Postal Service afloat, **not comprehensive reform**==. …

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the best title for the text?

options.A: The USPS Starts to Miss Its Good Old Days

questions.answerZh: 邮政服务需要的不仅仅是创可贴
basis: 全文先说美国邮政连年亏损、濒临破产，根源在需求下降和僵化的监管；利益集团阻挠改革。现在各方终于就法案达成一致，但最后一段说它只是让邮政勉强维持下去的最低限度措施，不是全面改革。Band-Aid（创可贴）比喻权宜之计，邮政需要的不只是创可贴，而是真正的改革。
map: the bare, bare minimum … not comprehensive reform
The Postal Service Needs More Than a Band-Aid

wrong.text: 原文没说邮政怀念过去的好日子。
利益集团保护自己的“奶酪”只是第二段的内容，不是全文中心。
作者批评的正是眼下的快速补救，主张全面改革，不是要快速治疗。

context.text: Americans are ==willing to **tolerate time-consuming security procedures** in return for increased safety==. The crash of EgyptAir Flight 804, which terrorists may have downed over the Mediterranean Sea, ==provides **another tragic reminder of why**==. …

questions.stem: The crash of EgyptAir Flight 804 is mentioned to ______.

options.A: stress the urgency to strengthen security worldwide
options.B: explain American’s tolerance of current security checks
options.C: highlight the necessity of upgrading major U.S. airports
options.D: emphasize the importance of privacy protection

questions.answerZh: 解释美国人对当前安检的容忍
basis: 第二段：美国人愿意忍受费时的安检程序（tolerate time-consuming security procedures）来换取更高的安全。埃及航空 804 航班可能被恐怖分子击落，这场悲剧再次提醒人们为什么（another tragic reminder of why）。why 承接上句，空难的例子是用来解释美国人为什么能容忍现行的安检。
map: tolerate time-consuming security procedures / reminder of why
explain American’s tolerance of current security checks

wrong.text: 空难说明的是航空旅行的安全风险，原文没有上升到加强全球安全，更没有呼吁其紧迫性。
第五段说预检计划不需要改造机场，针对的是安检费时，与空难无关。
第二段末的 private lives 指浪费时间拖累私人生活，与隐私保护无关。

context.text: … Enhanced security measures since then, ==combined with **a rise in airline travel**== due to the improving economy and low oil prices, ==**have resulted in** long waits at major airports== such as Chicago’s O’Hare International. …

questions.stem: Which of the following contributes to long waits at major airports?

options.B: The declining efficiency of the TSA.
options.C: An increase in the number of travelers.

questions.answerZh: 旅客数量的增加
basis: 第三段：自那以后加强的安全措施，加上经济好转、油价低带来的航空出行增加（a rise in airline travel），导致（have resulted in）主要机场等候时间过长。题干的 contributes to long waits 对应 have resulted in long waits，航空出行增加就是旅客数量增加。
map: a rise in airline travel
An increase in the number of travelers.

wrong.text: 第四段说的是乘客把随身行李塞得太多，不是对随身行李有新限制。
