context.text: … A lack of formal education, however, doesn’t constrain the ability of the developing world’s workforce to substantially improve productivity for the foreseeable future. On the contrary, ==**constraints on improving productivity** explain why education isn’t developing more quickly there== than it is.

questions.stem: According to the last paragraph, development of education ______.

options.B: does not depend on economic performance
options.C: follows improved productivity

questions.answerZh: 紧随生产率的提高之后
basis: 末段最后一句说，生产率提高受到的限制（constraints on improving productivity）解释了为什么那里的教育发展得不够快。换言之，生产率提高了，教育才会发展，即教育发展跟在生产率提高之后，这也与全文“经济发展促进教育”的观点一致。
map: constraints on improving productivity explain why education isn’t developing more quickly
follows improved productivity

wrong.text: 原文说竞争环境促使祖先发挥生产潜力，之后才有能力接受更多教育，是间接关系，不是“直接”促成。
全文认为经济（生产率）发展促进教育发展，选项说教育不依赖经济表现，与原文相反。
原文说政治变革可能只有在更广泛的正规教育下才能实现，选项把 afford 和 political changes 拼凑起来，意思不对。

context.text: … According to the standard history of American philosophy, ==**nowhere else** in colonial America== was “==**so much importance** attached to intellectual pursuits==.” …

questions.stem: The author holds that in the seventeenth-century New England ______.

options.C: politics benefited much from intellectual endeavors
options.D: intellectual pursuits enjoyed a liberal environment

questions.answerZh: 知识兴趣受到鼓励
basis: 根据题干 seventeenth-century New England 定位到第一段。第二句说，在美洲殖民地中没有哪个地方（nowhere else）像新英格兰那样重视知识追求（so much importance attached to intellectual pursuits）。如此重视知识追求，说明那里的文化、知识兴趣受到鼓励。
map: nowhere else in colonial America was “so much importance attached to intellectual pursuits”
intellectual interests were encouraged

wrong.text: 首段末句说清教传统主导的是美国的精神生活（intellectual life），不是政治生活。
文中只提到政治领袖（political leaders），没说政治从文化活动中受益。
原文只说新英格兰重视知识追求，推不出“享有自由的环境”；B 才是 D 成立的前提。

context.text: To take this approach to the New Englanders normally means to start with the Puritans’ theological innovations and their distinctive ideas about the church—important subjects that we may not neglect. But in keeping with our examination of southern intellectual life, we may ==consider the original Puritans as **carriers of European culture**==, ==adjusting to **New World** circumstances==. The New England colonies were the scenes of important episodes in the pursuit of widely understood ideals of civility and virtuosity.

questions.stem: It is suggested in Paragraph 2 that New Englanders ______.

options.A: experienced a comparatively peaceful early history
options.B: brought with them the culture of the Old World
options.C: paid little attention to southern intellectual life

questions.answerZh: 带来了旧大陆的文化
basis: 第二段第二句说，我们可以把最初的清教徒看作欧洲文化的承载者（carriers of European culture），他们在新大陆适应新的环境（adjusting to New World circumstances）。相对于新大陆，欧洲就是旧大陆，B 项是 carriers of European culture 的同义改写。
map: the original Puritans as carriers of European culture
brought with them the culture of the Old World

wrong.text: 第二段末句说新英格兰殖民地发生了许多重要事件，文中没说早期历史相对和平。
southern intellectual life 是作者自己对南部的考察，与新英格兰人是否关注南部无关。
第二段只是说研究新英格兰人通常从清教徒的神学创新入手，推不出他们沉迷于宗教创新。

context.text: … ==These men wrote and **published extensively**==, reaching both New World and Old World audiences, and ==giving New England an **atmosphere of intellectual earnestness**==.

questions.stem: The early ministers and political leaders in Massachusetts Bay ______.

options.A: were famous in the New World for their writings
options.B: gained increasing importance in religious affairs
options.C: abandoned high positions before coming to the New World
options.D: created a new intellectual atmosphere in New England

questions.answerZh: 在新英格兰创造了一种新的知识氛围
basis: 第三段先介绍马萨诸塞湾早期移民中的牧师和政治领袖，末句说这些人（These men）大量著书出版（wrote and published extensively），读者遍及新旧大陆，为新英格兰带来了热切求知的氛围（an atmosphere of intellectual earnestness）。D 项是末句的同义改写。
map: giving New England an atmosphere of intellectual earnestness
created a new intellectual atmosphere in New England

wrong.text: reaching both New World and Old World audiences 说的是著作拥有读者，不是他们因著作在新大陆闻名。
原文说约90位牧师来到马萨诸塞的教会，没说他们在宗教事务中越来越重要。
来波士顿之前当过王室官员的只是约翰·温斯罗普一人，原文也没说他放弃了高位。

context.text: … ==Their thinking often had a traditional **superstitious** quality.== A tailor named John Dane, who emigrated in the late 1630s, left an account of his reasons for leaving England that is ==filled with **signs**==. Sexual confusion, economic frustrations, and religious hope—all came together in a decisive moment when he opened the Bible, told his father that ==the first line he saw would **settle his fate**==, and read the magical words …

questions.stem: The story of John Dane shows that less well-educated New Englanders were often ______.

options.C: puzzled by church sermons

questions.answerZh: 受到迷信的影响
basis: 第四段第三句是观点句：这些受教育较少的人，思想往往带有传统的迷信色彩（a traditional superstitious quality）。接着举约翰·戴恩的例子：他记述离开英国的理由时满是各种征兆（filled with signs），还对父亲说翻开《圣经》看到的第一行字将决定他的命运（would settle his fate）。例子是为了说明观点，即受教育较少的新英格兰人常常受迷信影响。
map: Their thinking often had a traditional superstitious quality
influenced by superstitions

wrong.text: religious hope 是对宗教怀有期望，不是被宗教信仰困扰。
末句“人们会好奇戴恩对精心诠释圣经的布道作何感想”是作者的评论，不是说他们对布道感到困惑。
economic frustrations 只是戴恩一个人的经历，而且故事要说明的是迷信，不是家庭收入。

context.text: The early settlers of Massachusetts Bay included ==men of **impressive education** and influence in England==. …
We should not forget, however, that ==most New Englanders were **less well educated**==. …

Meanwhile, ==many settlers had **slighter religious commitments** than Dane’s==, as one clergyman learned in confronting folk along the coast who mocked that they had not come to the New World for religion. “==Our main end was to **catch fish**==.”

questions.stem: The text suggests that early settlers in New England ______.

options.A: were mostly engaged in political activities
options.B: were motivated by an illusory prospect
options.C: came from different intellectual backgrounds
options.D: left few formal records for later reference

questions.answerZh: 来自不同的知识背景
basis: 第三段介绍受过良好教育的早期移民（men of impressive education）；第四段转而说大多数新英格兰人受教育较少（less well educated），思想带有迷信色彩；第五段又说许多移民宗教信仰不那么虔诚（slighter religious commitments），来新大陆是为了捕鱼。可见早期移民来自不同的文化背景。
map: men of impressive education / most New Englanders were less well educated / slighter religious commitments
came from different intellectual backgrounds

wrong.text: 文中只提到少数政治领袖，大多数移民是工匠、农民等，并没有从事政治活动。
受《圣经》感召移民的只是约翰·戴恩这一类人，第五段说许多人是为了捕鱼（谋生）而来。
原文说受教育较少的工匠、农民很少留下文字作品，而受过良好教育的人大量著书出版，不能说早期移民都很少留下记录。

context.text: … “Women are ==**particularly susceptible** to developing depression and anxiety disorders== in response to stress compared to men,” according to Dr. Yehuda, chief psychiatrist at New York’s Veteran’s Administration Hospital.

Studies of both animals and humans have shown that ==**sex hormones** somehow affect the stress response==, causing females under stress to produce more of the trigger chemicals than do males under the same conditions. In several of the studies, when stressed-out female rats had their ovaries (the female reproductive organs) removed, ==their chemical responses **became equal** to those of the males==.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true according to the first two paragraphs?

options.A: Women are biologically more vulnerable to stress.
options.B: Women are still suffering much stress caused by men.
options.C: Women are more experienced than men in coping with stress.
options.D: Men and women show different inclinations when faced with stress.

questions.answerZh: 从生物学角度看，女性更容易受到压力的影响
basis: 第一段第二句说，与男性相比，女性在压力下特别容易（particularly susceptible）患抑郁症和焦虑症。第二段用研究说明原因：性激素（sex hormones）会影响压力反应，使处于压力下的雌性比雄性分泌更多诱发不良反应的化学物质；切除雌鼠卵巢后，其化学反应与雄鼠相同（became equal）。可见女性更易受压力伤害的根源在生理上，A 项是对前两段的概括：biologically 对应 sex hormones、ovaries，more vulnerable 对应 particularly susceptible。
map: particularly susceptible ... in response to stress / sex hormones somehow affect the stress response
biologically more vulnerable to stress

wrong.text: 首句 catching up to men 是说女性在某些领域还在追赶男性，文中没说女性的压力是男性造成的。
way ahead 是反语，指女性在“易受压力伤害”这个不好的方面领先，不是更会应对压力。
第二段说的是两性分泌化学物质的量不同，是客观的生理反应，不是主观上的“倾向”不同。

context.text: Adding to a woman’s increased dose of stress chemicals, are ==her **increased “opportunities”** for stress==. “It’s not necessarily that women don’t cope as well. It’s just that ==they have **so much more** to cope with==,” says Dr. Yehuda. “Their capacity for tolerating stress may even be greater than men’s,” she observes, “it’s just that they’re ==dealing with **so many more things**== that they become worn out from it more visibly and sooner.”

questions.stem: Dr. Yehuda’s research suggests that women ______.

options.A: need extra doses of chemicals to handle stress
options.B: have limited capacity for tolerating stress
options.C: are more capable of avoiding stress

questions.answerZh: 面对更多的压力
basis: 第三段是耶胡达医生的观点：女性面临压力的“机会”增多（increased “opportunities” for stress）；未必是女性应对压力的能力不如男性，只是她们要应对的事情多得多（so much more to cope with）；她们承受压力的能力甚至可能更强，只是要处理的事情太多（so many more things），所以更早、更明显地疲惫不堪。D 项是对这一段的概括。
map: increased “opportunities” for stress / so much more to cope with / so many more things
are exposed to more stress

wrong.text: 首句说压力“机会”增多加重了女性体内压力化学物质的剂量，不是女性需要额外的化学物质来应对压力。
原文说未必是女性应对得不如男性，她们承受压力的能力甚至可能比男性强。
原文说的是女性“承受”压力的能力（tolerating stress），选项换成了“避免”压力。

context.text: Dr. Yehuda notes another difference between the sexes. “I think that the kinds of things that women are exposed to tend to be ==in more of a **chronic or repeated** nature==. Men go to war and are exposed to combat stress. Men are exposed to more acts of random physical violence. The kinds of interpersonal violence that women are exposed to tend to be in domestic situations, by, unfortunately, parents or other family members, and ==they tend not to be **one-shot deals**==. The wear-and-tear that comes from these longer relationships can be quite devastating.”

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 4, the stress women confront tends to be ______.

options.C: durable and frequent

questions.answerZh: 持久的和频繁的
basis: 第四段第二句说，女性面临的各种事情往往更具长期性或反复性（chronic or repeated）；后面又说女性遭受的人际暴力往往不是一次了事（not to be one-shot deals），这些长久关系带来的折磨可能极具破坏性。C 项 durable and frequent 是 chronic or repeated 的同义替换。
map: in more of a chronic or repeated nature
durable and frequent

wrong.text: domestic 符合原文，但 temporary 与 chronic、not one-shot deals 意思相反。
random physical violence 说的是男性面临的压力，不是女性的。
random 同样是描述男性面临的暴力；trivial 原文没有，女性的压力是“极具破坏性的”。

context.text: … “It’s the hardest thing to take care of a teenager, have a job, ==pay the rent, pay the car payment, and **pay the debt**==. ==I lived from **paycheck to paycheck**==.”

questions.stem: The sentence “I lived from paycheck to paycheck.” (Line 6, Para. 5) shows that ______.

options.A: Alvarez cared about nothing but making money
options.B: Alvarez’s salary barely covered her household expenses
options.C: Alvarez got paychecks from different jobs
options.D: Alvarez paid practically everything by check

questions.answerZh: 阿尔瓦雷兹的工资几乎不够支付她的家庭开支
basis: 所考句的上一句说，阿尔瓦雷兹要照顾十几岁的孩子、做一份工作、付房租、还车贷、还债（pay the rent, pay the car payment, and pay the debt），连用三个 pay 说明开支沉重。所考句与上句顺接，live from paycheck to paycheck 指“挣的钱刚够维持到下次发薪”，即收入勉强够付家庭开支。
map: pay the rent, pay the car payment, and pay the debt / I lived from paycheck to paycheck
salary barely covered her household expenses

wrong.text: 她拼命工作、读书是为了应对压力、摆脱困境，原文没说她只关心赚钱。
这是对 paycheck to paycheck 的字面误读；上一句说的是 have a job（一份工作）。
paycheck 指工资（支票），这句话说的是收入勉强够用，不是用支票付款。

context.text: While still catching up to men in some spheres of modern life, ==women appear to be way ahead in at least one **undesirable category**==. …
Dr. Yehuda notes ==**another difference** between the sexes==. …

Not everyone experiences the kinds of severe chronic stresses Alvarez describes. But ==**most women** today are coping with a lot of obligations==, with few breaks, and feeling the strain. Alvarez’s experience demonstrates the importance of finding ways to diffuse stress before it threatens your health and your ability to function.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the best title for the text?

options.A: Strain of Stress: No Way Out?
options.C: Stress Analysis: What Chemicals Say

questions.answerZh: 性别不平等：压力下的女性
basis: 首段通过男女对比提出现象：女性在一个不好的方面遥遥领先（way ahead in ... undesirable category），即更容易受压力伤害。第二至五段从生理（性激素）和社会（压力更多、更持久）两方面分析原因，第四段开头又说两性的另一个差别（another difference between the sexes）；末段指出大多数女性承担着许多责任、压力很大。全文围绕“两性在压力面前的不平等、女性处境不利”展开，D 项涵盖了 gender 和 women、stress 两个关键词。
map: way ahead in ... undesirable category / another difference between the sexes / most women ... feeling the strain
Gender Inequality: Women Under Stress

wrong.text: 全文重在指出现象、分析原因，末段还建议找方法缓解压力，并不是说压力无路可逃；也没有体现“女性”这个关键词。
“对压力的反应”只是第二段的内容，而且选项没有体现女性处于不利地位这一重点。
化学物质只是第二段的论据，全文的重点不是从化学物质角度分析压力。

context.text: ==It **used to be** so straightforward.== A team of researchers working together in the laboratory ==would **submit** the results of their research to a journal==. A journal editor would then remove the authors’ names and affiliations from the paper and ==send it to their **peers for review**==. Depending on the comments received, the editor would ==**accept** the paper for publication or decline it==. Copyright rested with the journal publisher, and researchers seeking knowledge of the results would have to subscribe to the journal.

questions.stem: In the first paragraph, the author discusses ______.

options.A: the background information of journal editing
options.B: the publication routine of laboratory reports
options.C: the relations of authors with journal publishers
options.D: the traditional process of journal publication

questions.answerZh: 期刊出版的传统流程
basis: 第一段首句说“过去（这件事）是那么简单直接”（It used to be so straightforward），接着用 would 依次叙述过去的流程：研究人员向期刊提交成果（submit）→ 编辑隐去作者信息、送同行评审（peers for review）→ 编辑决定是否发表（accept ... or decline）→ 版权归出版商、读者需订阅期刊。可见首句的 It 指传统的期刊出版过程，traditional 对应 used to 和 would。
map: It used to be so straightforward / submit ... send it to their peers for review ... accept the paper for publication
the traditional process of journal publication

wrong.text: 编辑送审、决定是否录用只是出版流程中的一环，不是“期刊编辑的背景信息”。
原文是 the results of their research（研究成果），不是实验报告；而且选项没有体现“传统的、过去的”。
作者和出版商只是流程中的两方，本段讲的是整个出版过程，不是二者的关系。

context.text: … The Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) has just issued a report ==describing the **far-reaching consequences** of this==. The report, by John Houghton of Victoria University in Australia and Graham Vickery of the OECD, ==**makes heavy reading** for publishers who have, so far, made handsome profits==. But it goes further than that. It signals a change in what has, until now, been a key element of scientific endeavour.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of the OECD report?

options.B: It introduces an effective means of publication.
options.C: It upsets profit-making journal publishers.

questions.answerZh: 它让营利性期刊出版商感到不安
basis: 根据 OECD report 定位到第二段。报告描述了科研成果免费获取的深远影响，其直接影响是：让迄今为止获得丰厚利润的出版商读起来心情沉重（makes heavy reading for publishers who have, so far, made handsome profits）。C 项 upsets 对应 makes heavy reading，profit-making journal publishers 对应 publishers who have ... made handsome profits。
map: makes heavy reading for publishers who have, so far, made handsome profits
upsets profit-making journal publishers

wrong.text: 提出质疑的是资助机构，质疑对象是靠政府资助的研究牟利的商业出版商，不是政府资助的研究，也不是报告的内容。
报告是描述（describing）免费获取的深远影响，没有“介绍一种有效的出版方式”。
原文说报告标志着科研中一个关键要素的变化（signals a change），没说它使科研受益匪浅。

context.text: No longer. The Internet—and pressure from funding agencies, who are questioning why commercial publishers are making money from government-funded research by restricting access to it—==is making **free access** to scientific results a reality==. …
The value of knowledge and the return on the public investment in research ==depends, in part, upon wide distribution and **ready access**==. …

questions.stem: According to the text, online publication is significant in that ______.

options.A: it provides an easier access to scientific results
options.B: it brings huge profits to scientific researchers
options.C: it emphasizes the crucial role of scientific knowledge
options.D: it facilitates public investment in scientific research

questions.answerZh: 它提供了获取科学成果的更便捷途径
basis: 第二段第二句说，互联网（以及资助机构的压力）正在使免费获取科研成果成为现实（making free access to scientific results a reality）；第三段首句说知识的价值和科研公共投资的回报部分取决于广泛传播和便捷获取（ready access）；第四段介绍的各种在线出版模式也以 open access 为核心。可见网络出版的意义在于让人们更容易获取科研成果。
map: making free access to scientific results a reality / ready access
provides an easier access to scientific results

wrong.text: 第二段说获得丰厚利润（handsome profits）的是出版商，不是科研人员。
第三段首句说知识的价值取决于传播和获取，不是网络出版强调了科学知识的作用。
原文说便捷获取有助于提高科研公共投资的回报（return），不是方便公众投资科研。

context.text: … There is open-access publishing, typically supported by ==asking the author (or his employer) to **pay for the paper** to be published==. …

questions.stem: With the open-access publishing model, the author of a paper is required to ______.

options.A: cover the cost of its publication
options.B: subscribe to the journal publishing it
options.C: allow other online journals to use it freely

questions.answerZh: 支付其出版费用
basis: 根据题干 open-access publishing 定位到第四段：开放出版模式通常靠要求作者（或其雇主）支付论文发表的费用（pay for the paper to be published）来维持。A 项 cover the cost of its publication 是这句话的同义改写。
map: asking the author (or his employer) to pay for the paper to be published
cover the cost of its publication

wrong.text: 订阅期刊是传统出版模式下读者（其他研究人员）要做的事，不是开放出版模式对作者的要求。
open access 是面向所有读者开放，文中没说允许其他在线期刊免费使用论文。
末句只说这些模式可能改变传统同行评审的形式，没说作者要在投稿前完成同行评审。

context.text: ==It **used to be** so straightforward.== …
==**No longer**.== …

==This is **now changing**.== According to the OECD report, some 75% of scholarly journals are now online. ==Entirely **new business models** are emerging==; three main ones were identified by the report’s authors. …

questions.stem: Which of the following best summarizes the text?

options.A: The Internet is posing a threat to publishers.
options.B: A new mode of publication is emerging.
options.C: Authors welcome the new channel for publication.
options.D: Publication is rendered easier by online service.

questions.answerZh: 一种新的出版模式正在出现
basis: 文章用 It used to be ... No longer ... This is now changing 的今昔对比展开：第一段讲传统的期刊出版过程；第二段说互联网正在使免费获取科研成果成为现实；第三、四段说大多数学术期刊已经上网，全新的商业模式正在出现（Entirely new business models are emerging）。全文关注的是科学出版的新方式，B 项最能概括全文。
map: It used to be ... No longer ... This is now changing / Entirely new business models are emerging
A new mode of publication is emerging

wrong.text: 出版商心情沉重只是新出版方式带来的影响之一，而且威胁来自免费获取的新趋势，不是互联网本身。
文中没有提到论文作者对新出版渠道的态度。
网络使获取科研成果更容易，选项换成了“出版更容易”，文中没这样说。

context.text: In the early 1960s Wilt Chamberlain was ==one of the **only three** players== in the National Basketball Association (NBA) listed at over seven feet. If he had played last season, however, ==he would have been **one of 42**==. The bodies playing major professional sports have changed dramatically over the years, and managers have been more than willing to adjust team uniforms to fit ==the growing numbers of **bigger, longer frames**==.

questions.stem: Wilt Chamberlain is cited as an example to ______.

options.A: illustrate the change of height of NBA players
options.B: show the popularity of NBA players in the U.S.
options.C: compare different generations of NBA players
options.D: assess the achievements of famous NBA players

questions.answerZh: 说明NBA球员身高的变化
basis: 第一段前两句说，20世纪60年代初张伯伦是NBA中仅有的三名身高超过7英尺的球员之一（one of the only three players），如果他上个赛季还在打球，就只是42人中的一个（one of 42）。第三句接着说职业运动员的身材发生了巨大变化，身材更高大的球员越来越多（bigger, longer frames）。可见作者以张伯伦为例，是为了说明NBA球员身高的变化。
map: one of the only three players ... he would have been one of 42
illustrate the change of height of NBA players

wrong.text: 文中没有提到NBA球员在美国的受欢迎程度。
首段对比的是不同时期球员的身高，不是笼统地比较几代球员。
文中没有评价张伯伦等著名球员的成就。

context.text: Growth, which rarely continues beyond the age of 20, ==demands **calories and nutrients**==—notably, protein—to feed expanding tissues. At the start of the 20th century, ==under-nutrition and childhood infections **got in the way**==. But ==as **diet and health** improved==, children and adolescents have, on average, increased in height by about an inch and a half every 20 years …

questions.stem: Which of the following plays a key role in body growth according to the text?

options.C: Living standards.

questions.answerZh: 生活水平
basis: 第三段首句说身高增长需要热量和营养（calories and nutrients），尤其是蛋白质；接着对比：20世纪初营养不良和儿童期感染阻碍了身高增长（got in the way），后来随着饮食和健康状况的改善（diet and health improved），儿童和青少年每20年平均长高约1.5英寸。热量、营养、饮食、健康都属于生活水平，所以生活水平在身高增长中起关键作用。
map: calories and nutrients / under-nutrition / diet and health improved
Living standards

wrong.text: 第四段说基因结构对身高有限制，文中没提到基因改造。
第二段 environmental level 指生活环境水平，选项换成了“自然环境”。
文中没有提到日常锻炼。

context.text: … Moreover, even though humans have been upright for millions of years, ==our feet and back continue to struggle with **bipedal posture**== and cannot easily withstand repeated strain imposed by oversize limbs. “There are ==some **real constraints**== that are set by the genetic architecture of the individual organism,” says anthropologist William Leonard of Northwestern University.

questions.stem: On which of the following statements would the author most probably agree?

options.A: Non-Americans add to the average height of the nation.
options.B: Human height is conditioned by the upright posture.
options.C: Americans are the tallest on average in the world.
options.D: Larger babies tend to become taller in adulthood.

questions.answerZh: 人类身高受到直立姿势的制约
basis: 第四段第三句说，人类虽然直立行走了几百万年，双脚和背部仍在努力适应两足直立的姿势（struggle with bipedal posture），难以承受过大肢体反复施加的压力；接着引用人类学家的话：生物个体的基因结构确实设定了一些限制（real constraints）。可见直立姿势制约了人类身高，B 项 conditioned by 对应 constraints，the upright posture 对应 bipedal posture。
map: struggle with bipedal posture ... some real constraints
Human height is conditioned by the upright posture

wrong.text: 第二段说从世界各地招募球员提高了NBA球员的身高，选项把NBA球员换成了全美国人。
文中只说美国人身高已达极限，没说美国人是世界上平均身高最高的。
第四段只说较大的婴儿分娩时更难通过产道，没说他们成年后更高。

context.text: … She says that, unlike those for basketball, ==the length of military uniforms **has not changed** for some time==. And if you need to predict human height in the near future to design a piece of equipment, Gordon says that by and large, “==you could use **today’s data** and feel fairly confident==.”

questions.stem: We learn from the last paragraph that in the near future ______.

options.A: the garment industry will reconsider the uniform size
options.B: the design of military uniforms will remain unchanged
options.C: genetic testing will be employed in selecting sportsmen
options.D: the existing data of human height will still be applicable

questions.answerZh: 现有的人类身高数据仍然适用
basis: 最后一段说军服的尺寸已经很久没有改变（has not changed for some time）；末句说如果要为设计设备而预测不久将来的人类身高，完全可以用今天的数据，而且相当有把握（use today’s data and feel fairly confident）。D 项是末句的概括。
map: if you need to predict human height in the near future ... you could use today’s data
the existing data of human height will still be applicable

wrong.text: 原文说90%的制服无需改动就适合新兵，选项却说要重新考虑尺码；而且原文说的是军服，不是服装业。
原文说的是军服的长度（length）一段时间以来没有改变，不是军服设计将来保持不变。
文中没有提到用基因检测选拔运动员。

context.text: The trend in sports, though, may be obscuring an unrecognized reality: ==Americans have generally **stopped growing**==. Though typically about two inches taller now than 140 years ago, today’s people—especially those born to families who have lived in the U.S. for many generations—==apparently **reached their limit** in the early 1960s==. And they aren’t likely to get any taller. …
… “There are some real constraints that are ==set by the **genetic architecture** of the individual organism==,” says anthropologist William Leonard of Northwestern University.
==Genetic maximums can change, but **don’t expect** this to happen soon==. …

questions.stem: The text intends to tell us that ______.

options.A: the change of human height follows a cyclic pattern
options.B: human height is becoming even more predictable
options.C: Americans have reached their genetic growth limit
options.D: the genetic pattern of Americans has altered

questions.answerZh: 美国人已经达到了他们的基因生长极限
basis: 第二段首句是全文主旨：美国人总体上已经停止长高（stopped growing），在20世纪60年代初就达到了极限（reached their limit）；第三段说平均身高自1960年以来没有变化；第四段说明原因是基因结构设定的限制（genetic architecture）；第五段说基因最大值可能改变，但不会很快改变。C 项概括了全文。
map: Americans have generally stopped growing / reached their limit / genetic architecture
Americans have reached their genetic growth limit

wrong.text: 第三段只说20世纪初身高增长受阻、后来增长、1960年后停止，并不是循环模式。
末段说可以用今天的数据预测身高，是为了强调身高不再增长，不是说身高越来越容易预测。
末段说基因最大值可能会变，但不要指望很快发生，选项说基因模式已经改变。

context.text: In 1784, five years before he became president of the United States, George Washington, 52, was nearly toothless. So ==he hired a dentist to **transplant nine teeth** into his jaw==—having extracted them from the mouths of his slaves.
That’s ==a **far different image** from the cherry-tree-chopping George most people remember== from their history books. …

questions.stem: George Washington’s dental surgery is mentioned to ______.

options.A: show the primitive medical practice in the past
options.B: demonstrate the cruelty of slavery in his days
options.C: stress the role of slaves in the U.S. history
options.D: reveal some unknown aspect of his life

questions.answerZh: 揭示他生活中某个不为人知的方面
basis: 第一段讲华盛顿请牙医把从奴隶口中拔下的九颗牙移植到自己嘴里（transplant nine teeth）。第二段首句说，这与大多数人从历史书上记住的那个砍樱桃树的华盛顿形象大不相同（a far different image）。可见作者提到牙齿手术，是为了揭示华盛顿不为人知的一面。
map: a far different image from the cherry-tree-chopping George most people remember
reveal some unknown aspect of his life

wrong.text: 文中没有评价当时的医疗水平，这一项和第二段首句也接不上。
这个事例的主角是华盛顿，意在展示他鲜为人知的一面，不是论证奴隶制的残忍。
事例最多说明奴隶与华盛顿那一代人的关系，选项扩大到奴隶在整个美国历史上的作用。

context.text: … Works of several historians reveal ==the **moral compromises** made by the nation’s early leaders== and ==the **fragile nature** of the country’s infancy==. More significantly, they argue that many of the Founding Fathers knew slavery was wrong—and yet most did little to fight it.

questions.stem: We may infer from the second paragraph that ______.

options.A: DNA technology has been widely applied to history research
options.B: in its early days the U.S. was confronted with delicate situations
options.C: historians deliberately made up some stories of Jefferson’s life
options.D: political compromises are easily found throughout the U.S. history

questions.answerZh: 美国在建国初期面临着微妙的局势
basis: 第二段倒数第二句说，几位历史学家的著作揭示了美国早期领导人做出的道德妥协（moral compromises），以及国家建立初期的脆弱（the fragile nature of the country’s infancy）；末句说许多开国元勋知道奴隶制是错的，却很少采取行动反对它。可见美国建国初期处境微妙，B 项 delicate 对应 fragile，in its early days 对应 the country’s infancy。
map: the fragile nature of the country’s infancy
in its early days the U.S. was confronted with delicate situations

wrong.text: 原文只说1998年的DNA证据促使历史学家关注奴隶制，没说DNA技术已广泛用于历史研究。
DNA证据几乎证实了杰斐逊和奴隶有孩子，历史学家并没有编造故事。
原文说的是建国初期领导人的道德妥协，选项扩大成整个美国历史上随处可见政治妥协。

context.text: … While Washington and Jefferson ==privately expressed **distaste** for slavery==, they also understood that it was ==part of the political and economic **bedrock**== of the country they helped to create.
… Once in office, ==Jefferson **extended slavery** with the Louisiana Purchase== in 1803; the new land was carved into 13 states, including three slave states.
Still, ==Jefferson **freed** Hemings’s children==—though not Hemings herself or his approximately 150 other slaves. …

questions.stem: What do we learn about Thomas Jefferson?

options.A: His political view changed his attitude towards slavery.
options.B: His status as a father made him free the child slaves.
options.C: His attitude towards slavery was complex.
options.D: His affair with a slave stained his prestige.

questions.answerZh: 他对奴隶制的态度是复杂的
basis: 第三段说杰斐逊私下表达过对奴隶制的反感（distaste for slavery），但也明白奴隶制是国家政治经济基础的一部分（bedrock）；第五段说他上任后通过路易斯安那购地扩大了奴隶制（extended slavery）；第六段说他解放了海明斯的孩子，却没有解放海明斯本人和其他约150名奴隶。这些信息说明杰斐逊对奴隶制的态度是复杂的。
map: privately expressed distaste for slavery ... extended slavery ... freed Hemings’s children—though not Hemings herself
His attitude towards slavery was complex

wrong.text: 第五段说政治家的政治生涯依赖奴隶制，不是他的政治观点改变了他对奴隶制的态度。
他只解放了海明斯的孩子，选项扩大成“儿童奴隶”，文中也没说是父亲身份促使他这样做。
第二段只说DNA证据几乎证实他和奴隶有孩子，没说这件事玷污了他的声望。

context.text: And ==the statesmen’s **political lives depended** on slavery==. The three-fifths formula ==handed Jefferson his **narrow victory**== in the presidential election of 1800 by inflating the votes of the southern states in the Electoral College. …

questions.stem: Which of the following is true according to the text?

options.A: Some Founding Fathers benefit politically from slavery.
options.B: Slaves in the old days did not have the right to vote.
options.C: Slave owners usually had large savings accounts.
options.D: Slavery was regarded as a peculiar institution.

questions.answerZh: 一些开国元勋从奴隶制中获得了政治利益
basis: 第五段首句说，政治家们的政治生涯依赖奴隶制（political lives depended on slavery）；第二句举例：五分之三条款增加了南方各州在选举团中的票数，使杰斐逊在1800年总统选举中险胜（handed Jefferson his narrow victory）。可见一些开国元勋在政治上得益于奴隶制。
map: the statesmen’s political lives depended on slavery / handed Jefferson his narrow victory
Some Founding Fathers benefit politically from slavery

wrong.text: 第四段的五分之三条款是为了计算国会代表名额，文中没有提到奴隶有没有选举权。
“拥有奴隶就像拥有一大笔银行存款”是比喻，说奴隶对奴隶主价值很大，不是说奴隶主都有大笔存款。
the “peculiar institution” 加了引号，是南方各州对奴隶制的称呼，不是普遍的看法。

context.text: … Washington, who ==had begun to believe that **all men were created equal**== ==after observing the **bravery of the black soldiers** during the Revolutionary War==, overcame the strong opposition of his relatives to grant his slaves their freedom in his will. …

questions.stem: Washington’s decision to free slaves originated from his ______.

options.C: financial conditions

questions.answerZh: 军事经验
basis: 根据题干 Washington’s decision to free slaves 定位到最后一段第二句：华盛顿在独立战争中目睹黑人士兵的勇敢（after observing the bravery of the black soldiers during the Revolutionary War）之后，开始相信人人生而平等，于是不顾亲属强烈反对，在遗嘱中给了奴隶自由。促使他做出这一决定的是他的战争经历，即军事经历。
map: after observing the bravery of the black soldiers during the Revolutionary War
military experience

wrong.text: 第二段说的是开国元勋们在奴隶制问题上做出了道德妥协（moral compromises），选项把它反过来说成华盛顿出于道德考虑。
第四段说奴隶像一大笔银行存款，意思是奴隶主出于经济原因舍不得放弃奴隶，不能说明华盛顿因经济状况而释放奴隶。
第五段说政治家的政治生涯依赖奴隶制，讲的是杰斐逊等人的政治利益，与华盛顿释放奴隶无关。
